Base-promoted regio- and diastereoselective synthesis of tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides via alkynyl enones†
Shaochan Zhou,<sup>a</sup> Haotian Zou,<sup>a</sup> Xianqiang Huang, \*<sup>a</sup> Jialin Qi \*<sup>a</sup> and Zhenghu Xu <sup>b,c</sup>

A novel base-promoted method for hydrophosphinylation of alkynyl enones with secondary phosphine oxides has been developed. Using inexpensive and commercially available potassium carbonate, a variety of functionalized tri-substituted allene products were synthesized with exclusive regio- and diastereoselectivity under mild conditions. Furthermore, a one-pot, two-step, three-component tandem hydrophosphinylation/Heck reaction eficiently produced tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides in excellent yields, demonstrating a relatively broad substrate scope.

Allenes and their derivatives represent a distinct class of organic compounds that have garnered significant interest in recent years.<sup>1–4</sup> In particular, tri- and tetra-substituted allene compounds containing various functionalities (Scheme 1a) are receiving increasing attention due to their presence in numerous bioactive molecules.<sup>5–8</sup> As a result, several efective synthetic methodologies for multi-substituted allenes have been developed.<sup>9–16</sup> Among these synthons, alkynyl enones are readily accessible, versatile building blocks developed by Larock,<sup>17</sup> Zhan g,<sup>18–21</sup> and others.<sup>22–26</sup> 1,4-Addition to alkynyl enones provides a novel and eficient strategy for accessing functionalized allenes.<sup>27–34</sup> Xu et $a l . ^ { 3 2 }$ established a coppercatalyzed 1,4-protosilylation of α-alkynylenones to form functionalized chiral homoallenylsilanes (Scheme 1b, left). $\mathrm { Y a n g ^ { 3 1 } }$ achieved the synthesis of tri-substituted allenes through asymmetric additions of oxazolones to enynones, facilitated by chiral phosphoric acid (CPA) catalysis (Scheme 1b, right). Despite these significant contributions, there appears to be no reported instance of a 1,4-addition reaction utilizing alkynyl enones with a phosphorus nucleophile to synthesize homoallenyl phosphines.

On the other hand, organophosphorus motifs have been extensively employed in the design of chiral ligands and catalysts, as well as in medicinal and materials chemistry.<sup>35–40</sup> Hydrophosphinylation of unsaturated carbon–carbon bonds have emerged as direct and eficient strategies for constructing structures that incorporate both allenes and organophosphorus groups.<sup>41–56</sup> Recently, $\mathrm { H e } ^ { 4 7 }$ reported the reactions of α-hydroxyalkylphosphonates, acting as masked phosphonating reagents, with 1,3-enynes producing disubstituted allenes. Additionally, Ding’s group<sup>48</sup> developed a visible-light-induced radical-polar crossover 1,4-hydrophosphinylation of 1,3- enynes, enabling the formation of trisubstituted allenes featuring a phosphine oxide group. Several previous studies have attempted to establish diastereoselective processes related to the synthesis of homoallenyl phosphines. However, they typically resulted in 1 : 1 diastereoselectivity for the transformation.

Thus, we aim to accomplish regio- and diastereoselective synthesis of multi-substituted homoallenyl phosphines. Given the importance of multi-substituted allenes and organophosphorus compounds, along with our focus on the transformation of alkynyl enones,<sup>22</sup> we have designed a hydrophosphinylation reaction using alkynyl enones and secondary phosphine oxides to generate tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphines(Scheme 1c).

Alkynyl enone 1a and diphenylphosphine oxide 2a were selected to evaluate the viability of this hypothesis without any additives. In our preliminary test, the reaction successfully occurred using DCM as the solvent at room temperature (entry 1, Table 1), and the desired tri-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxide was isolated in 25% yield without diastereoselectivity (3a/3a′ = 50/50). Encouraged by this initial result, we proceeded with screening various bases to improve both the yield and diastereoselectivity of the reaction. Both organic and inorganic bases were efective in facilitating the reaction, providing products in good to excellent yields (entries 2–4). The type and amount of base were found to significantly influence diastereoselectivity. When 4 equivalents of $\mathbf { { K } } _ { 2 } \mathbf { { C O } } _ { 3 }$ were used, the product was isolated in 92% yield with the best diastereoselectivity (88/12 dr). Reducing the equivalents of base or 2a resulted in diminished yield and diastereoselectivity (entries 5–7). Solvent screening revealed that DCM remained the best solvent (entries 8–10). When THF was used as the solvent, another diastereomer, 3a′, emerged as the major product, but the yield dropped sharply to 34% (entry 8). At present, we have not achieved satisfactory results for the isomer 3a′ (for additional optimization results, see the ESI†).

text: Following the establishment of optimised conditions, the substrate scope of base-promoted hydrophosphinylation was next investigated. As summarized in Table 2, the scope is quite broad, with reactions requiring 26 hours and yielding the corresponding tri-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides in good to excellent yields with good diastereoselectivities. First, the reactivities of various alkynyl enones were examined. Diverse halogens, such as F, Cl, and Br, as well as electrondonating groups like $\mathrm { C H } _ { 3 } , \mathrm { O C H } _ { 3 }$ and OTs were well tolerated in this reaction. Substrates containing a 2-naphthyl group (3i) and heterocycles such as thienyl (3f) were also compatible with the transformation, delivering corresponding allenes in 59% and 52% yields respectively. When the substituent (R<sup>2</sup>) on the ketone moiety was replaced with a methyl-substituted ketone (2l), the corresponding product 3l was obtained in an excellent yield (94%) with 57/43 diastereoselectivity. Next, a series of substituted diaryl phosphine oxides were studied to evaluate the potential for synthetic elaboration under the optimal conditions. Electron-donating substituents on the phenyl rings were compatible, yielding products (3m–3o) with 84%–98% yields and diastereomeric ratios of 56 : 44 to 78 : 22.

Subsequently, a novel one-pot, two-step, three-component tandem hydrophosphinylation/Heck reaction was developed.<sup>57–59</sup> This reaction involves electron-deficient enynes, secondary phosphine oxides, and aryl halides to provide highly functionalized tetrasubstituted allenes (Table 3). However, the complex reaction system, characterized by numerous byproducts, an elusive reaction mechanism, and poor reaction eficiency, makes this process quite challenging. The intermolecular nucleophile, diaryl phosphine oxides, initially attacks to form an allenyl intermediate. Subsequently, the potential reaction pathway depends on the Lewis acidity of the ArPdX species generated by the oxidative addition of aryl halides with a $\operatorname { P d } ( 0 )$ catalyst. By utilising Lewis acid catalysis, several tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides were successfully synthesised.

Herein, we report the Heck reaction of allenes, produced by hydrophosphinylation of alkynyl enones, carried out at 80 °C catalysed by 5 mol% $\mathrm { P d } ( \mathrm { P P h } _ { 3 } ) _ { 4 }$ in the presence of $\mathbf { { K } } _ { 2 } \mathbf { { C O } } _ { 3 }$ (4.0 equiv.) as a base (Table 3). The coupling reaction between 2a and 4a is performed,<sup>60–62</sup> therefore a one-pot approach is employed to progressively add reaction reagents, ensuring that the cascade reaction proceeds in a controlled manner. After careful optimization, reducing the loading of diphenylphosphine oxide to 1.5 equiv. and raising the reaction temperature to ${ 9 0 } \ { ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } } ,$ the desired tetrasubstituted allene 5a was isolated in 80% yield. As illustrated in Table 4, a variety of structurally interesting tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides were obtained in good yields, and the structure of 5c was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray difraction analysis.

Notably, the family of 8 has been reported to possess antimicrobial,<sup>64</sup> antiinflammatory,<sup>65</sup> antimalarial,<sup>66</sup> hypolipidemic,<sup>67</sup> and analgesic activities.<sup>68</sup> To elucidate the mechanism and operative pathway of the diastereoselective 1,4-hydrophosphinylation reaction, we conducted mechanistic experiments. Monitoring the reaction progress revealed that alkynyl enones 1a essentially completed the hydrophosphinylation reaction in about 6 hours, giving only 50 : 50 diastereoselectivity. Subsequently, with the aid of the base $\mathbf { K } _ { 2 } \mathbf { C O } _ { 3 } ,$ the dr value gradually increased, with the optimum result achieved at 26 hours (Scheme 2b). After this point, the diastereoselectivity decreased precipitously, so we controlled the reaction time of alkynyl enones and diarylphosphineoxides to 26 h and tested diastereoselective transformations of tri-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxide 3a in the presence of a base using a single isomer (Scheme 2c). The decline in dr value of tri-substituted allenes over time serves as a significant indication of the pivotal role that the base plays in the hydrophosphinylation.

Based on the experimental results outlined above, the proposed mechanism is depicted in Scheme 3. Initially, R<sub>2</sub>P(O)H is deprotonated to form the phosphoryl anion A in the presence of a base. This anion then undergoes the 1,4-addition reaction with the alkynyl enone, generating the allenyl carbanion intermediate B. Intermediate B can extract a proton (H<sup>+</sup>) from SPOs, leading to the formation of the tri-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxide 3 and the regeneration of the phosphoryl anion A. The two-component product 3 can then undergo the Heck reaction with an aryl iodide in the presence of Pd(0). The resulting aryl palladium(II) intermediate C, formed via the oxidative addition of iodobenzene, undergoes the migratory insertion with compound 3, forming the allyl– Pd complex D. Finally, the β-H elimination reaction occurs, yielding the tetra-substituted homologous phosphine oxide 5 and product E.

In summary, we have successfully developed an eficient 1,4- addition of alkynyl enones under mild conditions, providing tri- and tetra-substituted homoallenyl phosphine oxides. Using only the inexpensive potassium carbonate, various functionalized tri-substituted allenes were generated in moderate to excellent yields with complete regio- and diastereoselectivity. A base-promoted and Pd(0)-catalyzed one-pot, two-step, threecomponent tandem hydrophosphinylation/Heck reaction of alkynyl enones, diarylphosphineoxides and aryl iodides resulted in tetra-substituted allenes. These simple and eficient methods further expand the synthetic potential of these scafolds in organic synthesis.
